solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top man realising some manoeuvring is required

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving pieces around, so the letters of the two words before it are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A leader realises that some tactical manoeuvring is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' rearranges REALISING SOME; 'is required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme commander of combined armed forces is the top military man, the highest rank of general.

clue.text: He votes for a European king

definitions.text: He votes for a European king

parts.words: He votes for a European king
parts.note: reads like any voter, but historically certain German princes held the right to choose the Holy Roman Emperor

explanation.walkthrough: The Holy Roman Emperor was chosen by a small college of German princes, each bearing this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who votes holds this title, and so did the princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor, effectively a European king.

clue.text: Forced to bring up the cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom to the top, so backwards

parts.note: to be forced to do something is to be made to do it

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to vomit after eating some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring up' turns MADE upwards in this down entry; the surface sense of vomiting is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, named after a town in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Ancient city where Syrians went to a chin-wag?

indicators.note: to wag is to move to and fro, so the letters of the words just before it are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An old Syrian city where the locals gathered for a good gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chin-wag' reads as a chat, but the hyphen splits it: CHIN joins TO A as fodder and 'wag' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A city of the ancient world on the Orontes, a great centre of Hellenistic and early Christian Syria.

clue.text: Apathy I retain, however moved

indicators.note: however it is moved suggests the letters before it can be arranged in any order

explanation.surface: Someone admits to staying apathetic, however emotionally moved they might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however moved' rearranges I RETAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish disinclination to act or change is a synonym for apathy or listlessness.

clue.text: Drains made up as an afterthought

indicators.note: in a down clue, made up means set upwards, so the word as is read from bottom to top

parts.note: PS, postscript, is the afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Drains are fitted to a building as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' turns 'as' upwards into SA in this down entry. 'Drains' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone's energy is to weaken or exhaust it, the verb sense of tapping off sap.

clue.text: Objecting to baby-sitting?

definitions.meaning: to object to something is to mind it, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the verb to mind: to object, and to look after or tend a child.

clue.text: Takes the plunge without consulting the directors

definitions.meaning: literally falls from a ship into the sea
going over the heads of the company board, bypassing its directors

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: acting over the board of directors; the usual idiom means acting to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling off a ship's side is the literal phrase; the second is a punning reading of the company board.

clue.text: His aim is to see that people settle

definitions.text: His aim is to see that people settle

parts.words: His aim is to see that people settle
parts.note: settle looks like making a home, but here it means paying off what is owed

explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' suggests settling down or settling disputes; it means settling accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to recover unpaid money wants people to settle their accounts.

clue.text: To carve cooked ham

indicators.note: cooked suggests the words have been doctored or falsified, so their letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Instructions for slicing a joint of cooked ham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TO CARVE. 'ham' looks like the meat but is the verb, to play a part too broadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform with exaggerated theatricality, the same as hamming it up on stage.

clue.text: Cost of stocking the river with birds

indicators.note: stocking a river means putting things into it, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Someone counts the outlay of filling a river with waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan; the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost incurred, money paid out for something.

clue.text: Sound sense of position

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for sense is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A remark about having a good sense of where things are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound sense' reads as good judgement; 'Sound' is the homophone signal on SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Lad about to return stolen property

indicators.note: about means around, so the lad goes around the other piece

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: A boy is on the point of handing back things he has stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns 'to' into OT. 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot or plunder taken by thieves or soldiers is booty, goods that have been stolen.

clue.text: Plant where workers strike for more money

definitions.text: where workers strike for more money
definitions.meaning: the place where coins are struck, producing more money

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on striking: not industrial action but stamping coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a fragrant herb, and the mint is the factory where coins are struck.

clue.text: Turf out? Of course

parts.note: turf out suggests evicting someone, but it means a piece of turf gouged out on a golf course

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turf out' looks like 'throw out'; it is a chunk of turf dug up by a golf club, and 'course' is the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's club often cuts a small lump of turf out of the course with the shot.

clue.text: Novel house, but starting to let rain in

indicators.note: starting means the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: a roof that lets rain in has a leak

explanation.surface: A house in a novel, though it is starting to let the rain in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' takes B from 'but'. Bleak House is a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is the Dickens novel, so the house in that title is the bleak one.

clue.text: Application for wood and nails

parts.note: wood and nails sound like carpentry materials, but nails are fingernails: one coating serves furniture and manicures

explanation.walkthrough: 'nails' suggests the hardware beside wood; it is fingernails, which take nail polish of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy coating applied to wooden surfaces, and the name of the polish painted on fingernails.

clue.text: Almost declare, with runs at Oval starting to be briskly scored

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to allege is to declare or assert
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: starting takes the first letter of the word next to it

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a side nearly declares, scoring runs quickly at the Oval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts ALLEGE to ALLEG; 'starting' gives O. The Oval is a London cricket ground, and 'scored' means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking for a lively, brisk pace, written into the score.

clue.text: It provides an opening for parachutists

definitions.text: It provides an opening for parachutists

parts.words: It provides an opening for parachutists
parts.note: an opening sounds like a chance or a door, but it is the opening of the canopy

explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' suggests an opportunity; it is the pulled line that opens the parachute.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling this line releases the pack so that the parachute opens.

clue.text: Picnic arranged to entertain posh composer

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece goes inside the other
arranged means set out in a new order, so the letters of picnic are reshuffled

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, an old label for posh usage

explanation.surface: A picnic laid on to entertain a classy composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges PICNIC into PCCINI, and 'to entertain' puts U inside it. U for upper-class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini was the Italian composer of La Bohème and Tosca.

clue.text: Form of art having spirit and propriety

parts.note: Art Deco is a style, or form, of art and design
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: An art form that combines vitality with good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, seemly behaviour, a synonym for propriety.

clue.text: The Spanish are after an adjustable clasp knife

indicators.note: are after places the Spanish article at the end, following the other piece
something adjustable can be altered or rearranged, so the letters of clasp are reordered

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Spaniards are hunting for a folding knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustable' rearranges 'clasp' into SCALP. 'clasp knife' reads as a folding knife, hiding the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small, very sharp surgical knife.

clue.text: News item — though a cert favourite comes last

indicators.note: comes last puts the favourite after the other piece

parts.note: a snip is a certainty, a sure thing, like a bargain
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A racing news item: though a horse was a certainty, the favourite came in last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cert' and 'favourite' suggest horse racing; SNIP is a racing term for a sure bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece of news or information.

clue.text: After the wine I join the company in the porch

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: After a glass of wine, I join the firm out on the porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'join' are links setting the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a roofed porch supported by columns at a building's entrance.

clue.text: Formerly of some concern

indicators.note: of some means part of the following word, a run of letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: Something that was once a matter of some concern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of some' takes a run of letters from within CONCERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, a synonym for formerly.

clue.text: A creditor I'd made bitter

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creditor I upset became bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link, not an anagram signal; 'A creditor' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharply bitter, especially of smell or taste.

clue.text: Cold anger makes him turn tail

indicators.note: to turn tail is to turn round and go back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Cold fury makes a man turn and run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn tail' turns CIRE round. 'him' stands for a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name, so 'him' can stand for any particular man such as this one.

clue.text: Yearn for each other

indicators.note: other signals a different form of the word before it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people yearn for one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each other' reads as a phrase; 'other' rearranges EACH and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to long or yearn for it.

clue.text: Flower goes to politician in ceremony

parts.note: a river is a flower in crosswords, something that flows; the Po is Italy's longest river
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A bloom is presented to a politician at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom but means a thing that flows, a river. 'goes to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour, display at a formal ceremony.

clue.text: U.S. coach right to oppose racial trouble

indicators.note: trouble means disturbance, so the letters of racial are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A right to oppose racial trouble in American coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges RACIAL into AILCAR; 'to oppose' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a railroad coach or carriage is called a railcar.

clue.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

definitions.text: It may qualify as part of an agreement

parts.words: It may qualify as part of an agreement
parts.note: qualify means to limit or attach a condition to, as a clause does within a contract

explanation.walkthrough: 'qualify' suggests passing a test; it means adding a condition or limit.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause in a contract that attaches a condition to it, qualifying the agreement.

clue.text: Iron out a bottleneck, for example

definitions.text: Iron out a bottleneck, for example

parts.words: Iron out a bottleneck, for example
parts.note: the phrase muddles two images, smoothing creases and narrowing a passage, which is the kind of figure of speech meant

explanation.walkthrough: Ironing smooths wrinkles; a bottleneck is a narrowing. Combining them clashes two images in one figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining two incompatible figures of speech, like ironing a bottleneck, is a classic example of this fault.
